title: Historical GCMT counts did not resolve an early-to-later distant earthquake contrast around 50 Mw 7.5+ events in 1982-1999
abstract: We tested whether an early distant earthquake count deficit in recent ComCat data could also be resolved in an earlier Global CMT period. Centers were 50 Mw 7.5+ events in 1982-1999. Neighbors had Mw at least 5.8 and surface distance above 1000 km. Mirrored 0-6 hour windows had one after and two before incidences. The 6-24 hour windows had 13 after and 17 before incidences. The early-minus-later after share was -0.100. A shared within-year time-shift test gave a lower-tail p value of 0.2803. The finite-draw 95% year-resampling interval was -0.625 to +0.594; 3.74% of draws were undefined. Removing one year at a time could reverse the point sign. Fixed distance, magnitude and isolation checks did not resolve a contrast. The sample has too few early incidences to confirm or refute transfer. This is an earlier-period catalog test informed by prior evidence, not a new physical suppression claim. It cannot identify missed detections or a recovery time. Catalog completeness, source revisions, dependence and conditional resampling limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate counts, simulation draws, an independent count audit and an original figure support reproduction. External catalog records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Historical distant counts and early-minus-later after share. The primary early window contains only three incidences. Intervals use defined year-resampling draws; undefined draws are reported in the text.
